//: CAUTIOUS preset (guide/10-permissions.md). Auto-approves READS ONLY; everything else prompts. Common read-only shell commands (ls, cat, grep, git status/log/diff, …) need no rule: Claude Code runs its built-in read-only set without prompting and STILL prompts for their write-capable forms. An explicit Bash allow rule would remove that protection (Bash(find *) also allows `find . -delete`). Best for a new setup, an unattended server, or while building trust. Copy the block into your CLI's settings.
//everythingElse: Not listed => prompts. All writes, all non-read shell, all network, all VC, all installs, all material actions require an explicit prompt.
